title: Writer: writing text ready for translation
when: The text will be translated (a bilingual site, an app with a language switch) and must be written so translation is easy and safe.
prompt:
Goal: Source text and string files that translate cleanly: full sentences, no concatenation, room for longer words, and clear context.
Steps:
1. Keep each message a full sentence with placeholders by name: "{count} items in your cart", never "items" glued to a number in code.
2. Avoid idioms, puns and cultural references; say "very easy" instead of a figure of speech.
3. Handle plurals as separate strings (one, other) instead of adding an s.
4. Store strings in one JSON file per language with the same keys (en.json, pt.json) and a short context note per key that is ambiguous.
5. Leave room: layouts must allow text about 30 percent longer; no text baked into images.
6. Write dates, numbers and currency through Intl formatting, not in the strings.
Quality bar:
- Every key exists in every language file.
- No sentence is built from fragments.
- Placeholders are named.
Pitfalls:
- Concatenated fragments whose word order breaks in other languages.
- The same English word used for two meanings under one key.
- Fixed width buttons that clip translations.
Verify:
- [ ] JSON files parse.
- [ ] Keys match across languages.
- [ ] Plurals handled.
- [ ] No text in images.
Output: One JSON strings file per language and any code patches that read them.

examples.output: en.json and pt.json with same keys, "cart.count": "{count} items", plurals one and other
